wave: CORRECTNESS -- R4.12's explicitly documented and tested guarantee ('a CALL argument/result PlaceRef converges on the EXACT SAME record_id DATA_FLOW's own pass produces') silently broke whenever the argument or let-result initializer was wrapped in `(..)` parentheses (both positions) or `&`/`&mut` (arguments only), even though DATA_FLOW's own walker still produces the corresponding Use/Definition record for exactly these shapes. A genuinely resolvable case was wrongly reported as PlaceRef::Unresolved.
wave_title: Twenty-seventh generation this cycle. Continuing the standing correctness priority after the R5 absorption/extinction objective and the prior CFG/dataflow scope-handling fixes. Delegated a background Explore survey of the CALL dimension's dispatch resolution logic (fresh, previously-unaudited territory in adapter/src/semantic/rust/mod.rs) -- it ruled out callee/dispatch classification, call-attribution/traversal order, and CALL-specific identity-collision bugs as genuinely sound and already well-tested, and found one real, precise gap in argument/result PlaceRef binding.
priority_classification: correctness -- an under-approximation (Unresolved is always a safe, non-fabricated answer, so this is not a false-positive class of bug), but a real, silent gap against an EXPLICITLY documented and tested invariant, reachable from the single most common way a non-trivial local gets passed by name in idiomatic Rust (`&x`).
gap_discovered_by: A background Explore subagent survey, scoped to CALL dispatch resolution after this session's earlier CFG/dataflow scope-handling fixes. Independently re-verified before acting: read place_ref_for_argument/walk_value_position_expr/place_ref_for_let_result/place_ref_for_assign_result directly in adapter/src/semantic/rust/mod.rs, read simple_path_ident directly in spelling.rs (confirmed its own doc comment explicitly excludes `(expr)`), and read dataflow.rs's real Expr::Paren/Expr::Reference arms directly to confirm DATA_FLOW itself DOES transparently unwrap both before emitting a Use -- the exact asymmetry the survey described.
key_finding: Three call sites share one root cause: CALL's argument/result recognizers (`place_ref_for_argument`, `walk_value_position_expr`, and transitively `place_ref_for_let_result`) check only an expression's literal top-level variant, with no unwrap step -- while DATA_FLOW's own recursive walker (`dataflow.rs`'s `Expr::Paren`/`Expr::Reference` arms) transparently descends through both before reaching the `Use`-emitting `Expr::Path` arm. `helper((x))`, `helper(&x)`, and `let y = (helper(x));` all still produce the corresponding real DATA_FLOW record, but CALL reported PlaceRef::Unresolved for all three. Confirmed by direct execution: independently constructed test fixtures for all three cases and ran them against the real, unfixed implementation, observing the exact described failure before any fix.
verification_before_acting: Read place_ref_for_argument, walk_value_position_expr, place_ref_for_let_result, place_ref_for_assign_result directly in adapter/src/semantic/rust/mod.rs, confirming the exact unwrap gap the survey described.

Read spelling::simple_path_ident directly, confirming its own doc comment explicitly names `(expr)` as an excluded shape, and confirming its claim of matching 'the exact structural shape dataflow.rs's Expr::Path arm recognizes' was accurate only for the arm ITSELF, not for every shape that ultimately reaches it through dataflow.rs's own prior unwrapping.

Read dataflow.rs's real Expr::Paren/Expr::Reference arms directly (lines 374, 376), confirming DATA_FLOW's own walker transparently descends through both before its Expr::Path arm emits a Use -- the asymmetry's other half.

Traced every real usage of simple_path_ident across the workspace (grep) before deciding the fix's scope: confirmed dataflow.rs's OWN Expr::Assign/compound-assign arms also call simple_path_ident directly on the LHS with no Paren-unwrapping either -- meaning `(y) = helper(x);` currently produces no Store record in DATA_FLOW at all (falls through to a differently-shaped, arguably-also-buggy generic walk). Deliberately did NOT extend the fix to place_ref_for_assign_result's Paren case: doing so would make CALL's result-binding MORE capable than DATA_FLOW's own current Store detection, reintroducing a divergence in the opposite direction rather than closing one. This asymmetric scoping (assignment-target Paren-unwrapping is a real, separate, lower-priority gap in dataflow.rs itself, not fixed this generation) was a deliberate design decision, not an oversight.
Confirmed via grep that no existing test in tests.rs (2000+ CALL-dimension test lines) used a Paren- or Reference-wrapped argument/result before writing new tests -- the gap was genuinely untested.

design_decisions.question: Fix simple_path_ident itself to unwrap Paren/Reference, or add a separate function?
design_decisions.decision: Added two new, narrowly-scoped helpers to spelling.rs (unwrap_parens: Paren-only, safe in any position; unwrap_value_read: Paren+Reference, value-read positions only) rather than changing simple_path_ident's own behavior. simple_path_ident is also used by dataflow.rs's own Assign/compound-assign LHS recognition (place positions), where unwrapping Reference would be actively WRONG (`&x = 5;` is never valid Rust as an assignment target -- unwrapping it there would fabricate a Store claim for invalid syntax). Keeping the two unwrap helpers separate and explicit about which positions each is safe for avoids that trap while still closing the real gap.

design_decisions.question: Should the argument-position fix also unwrap Expr::Reference, given place positions must not?
design_decisions.decision: Yes for place_ref_for_argument specifically: a call argument is always a value-READ position (never an assignable place), so unwrap_value_read (Paren+Reference) is safe and correct there. walk_value_position_expr's own Paren-unwrapping (for recognizing a wrapped call as a let/assign initializer) deliberately uses the Paren-only unwrap_parens, not unwrap_value_read: `let y = &helper(x);` binds y to a REFERENCE to the call's result, not to the result itself, so unwrapping the Reference there would be a genuine misattribution, not a fix.

stable_validator_law_compliance.claim: CALL's argument and let-result PlaceRef binding now correctly recognizes a `(..)`-wrapped (both positions) or `&`/`&mut`-wrapped (argument position only) simple identifier, converging on the exact same DATA_FLOW record_id a bare identifier would, closing a real gap against R4.12's own explicitly documented and tested convergence invariant.

overall_verdict: FOUND, FALSIFIED, FIXED, AND VERIFIED. R4.12's own explicitly documented and tested CALL-argument/result-to-DATA_FLOW convergence guarantee silently broke for parenthesized and reference-wrapped simple identifiers -- reachable from the single most common way a non-trivial local is passed by name in idiomatic Rust (&x). Closed with two narrowly-scoped, position-aware unwrap helpers, each independently confirmed real against the unfixed implementation before being trusted. A related, real gap in DATA_FLOW's own assignment-target Paren handling was identified, deliberately left unfixed to avoid inverting the convergence divergence, and named as a legitimate follow-up. Full workspace suite green (588/588, up from 585), clippy clean.
